entries.label: Long-run effect of the ETCR indicator on (Harrod-neutral) multifactor productivity
entries.units: change in ln MFP per index point of ETCR (0–6 scale)

citation.title: The quantification of structural reforms in OECD countries: A new framework
citation.publisher: OECD Economics Department Working Papers No. 1354, ECO/WKP(2016)78
citation.locator: Table 1, row 'ETCR aggregate', columns (1) and (3), p. 10 (PDF p. 11); simulation column, note to Figure 1, p. 15; caveat, para. 10, p. 8

entries.quote: ETCR aggregate -0.037** -0.047** -0.035** -0.025** … The estimates for the long- and short run effects of the policies and the convergence parameters are taken from column 3 of Table 1 and Table A4.1 for MFP … overall ETCR and barriers to entry have large standard errors for the full sample.
entries.derivation: Value = column (3), the column the paper uses in its simulations (−0.047). Low and high = columns (3) and (1), the two MFP specifications with ETCR aggregate (−0.047 and −0.037).
entries.notes: Both columns have country fixed effects only. With year fixed effects (column 2) the aggregate ETCR is not significant and only public ownership is (−0.027); the paper notes the large standard errors. ETCR covers energy, transport and communications only (A-P07). The paper's MFP is Harrod-neutral (labour-augmenting), so a shock built from this coefficient enters Layer B as labour-augmenting, or times (1 − α) if entered as Hicks-neutral (A-P18). Time path: entries layer-b.five-year-share.eg2016 and layer-b.ecm-mfp.eg2016.

entries.label: Long-run effect of the ETCR indicator on the capital–output ratio
entries.units: change in ln(K/Y) per index point of ETCR (0–6 scale)

citation.title: The quantification of structural reforms in OECD countries: A new framework
citation.publisher: OECD Economics Department Working Papers No. 1354, ECO/WKP(2016)78
citation.locator: Table 1, row 'ETCR aggregate', columns (4) and (5), p. 10 (PDF p. 11); para. 13, p. 9 (PDF p. 10)

entries.quote: ETCR aggregate -0.037** -0.047** -0.035** -0.025** … Product market regulation, measured by the ETCR indicator, shows a fairly robust negative relationship with the capital stock series.
entries.derivation: Low and high = the two capital-deepening specifications, columns (4) and (5) (−0.035 and −0.025); value = their midpoint (−0.030), because the paper does not say which column its simulations use.
entries.notes: Both columns have country and year fixed effects; column (5) adds labour market policies. K/Y enters GDP per head through α/(1 − α) in the paper's aggregation (α = 0.33).
